system_prompt: You are a careful game QA test designer. Return ONLY valid JSON. Generate executable test specifications, not test results. Never claim a test passed. SCOPE: CONTROLS ONLY. You test whether each player control works, NOT whether the game can be won, scored, lost or completed. Work in two steps. STEP 1: read the play manual and plan and list every player control (a key the player presses), what it does, and the exact console line the manual says the game prints when it takes effect. STEP 2: write exactly one test per control: start the game, wait if the control needs a moment to be valid, press that key, wait about 1 second, and expect that exact console line. Do not test game mechanics, scoring, collisions, enemies, win/lose conditions, visuals or level completion: leave those requirements out entirely.

files.purpose: Main game logic, including game loop, command parsing, and state management.

assets.strategy_rationale: The game is a text adventure, so all visual elements will be rendered as text directly in Pygame, not as images.

locations.summary: Defines the game's interconnected locations and their properties.
locations.detail: Each location will have a name, description, available items, and exits to other locations. The connections will be a dictionary mapping location names to another dictionary of directions and target locations. Special conditions for movement (e.g., lantern for dark tunnel, key for treasure room) will be handled during movement validation.

inventory_system.detail: A simple list or set to store items the player has picked up. The 'take' command adds items, and the 'inventory' command displays them. Items will be removed from the location once taken.

play_manual.notes:
Implementation notes and limitations:
- The game is a turn-based text adventure rendered in a Pygame window. Commands are typed into the window. Press Enter to submit a command. Backspace edits, Escape quits (prints QUIT).
- Exact console lines printed by the game when commands take effect (printed with flush=True):
  - look -> 'LOOK'
  - go <direction> (successful) -> 'MOVED <DIRECTION>' where <DIRECTION> is NORTH/SOUTH/EAST/WEST
  - go <direction> (blocked) -> 'BLOCKED'
  - take <item> (successful) -> 'TOOK <item>' (item name preserved as in world data, e.g., 'lantern', 'rusty key')
  - take <item> (not present) -> 'BLOCKED'
  - inventory -> 'INVENTORY'
  - help -> 'HELP'
  - quit or Escape -> 'QUIT' and the game exits
  - unknown command -> 'UNKNOWN COMMAND'
  - winning (entering treasure with rusty key) -> 'WIN' and the game exits
- After each command the game also updates on-screen text showing the confirmation and the current location description. Those on-screen lines are not duplicated to stdout except for the single confirmation line per command.
- Items are matched case-insensitively for 'take' commands.
- There is no in-game restart command; restart by re-running the program.
- The window title is 'Lantern Cave' per the Plan.
- Limitations: The on-screen UI is textual and minimal; no images are used. The game must be run with an interactive display; automated headless runs may not capture Pygame window interactions.
- Implementing files: game/lantern_cave.py (implements all gameplay, parsing, state and rendering), game/__init__.py (package marker).
- Controls (exact printed console lines) and how to trigger them are listed above.

controls.manual_quote: the exact manual sentence that states this key and its printed line

observation.target: the console line the play manual says this control prints

generation_notes: which controls were found, and any control that could not be tested and why

constraints: Fill 'controls' first (STEP 1), then 'tests' (STEP 2). One test per control, test_ids C01, C02, ...
Only list a control if the play manual names the key AND the exact console line it prints. Put the supporting manual sentence in manual_quote. Never invent a printed line.
Each test's 'expected' must be exactly the control's 'prints' line, and observation.method must be stdout.
For a terminal (text) game a control is a typed command: use {"type": "input", "text": "go north"} (the validator adds the Enter) and put the command in the control's key field.

Actions: press / key_down / key_up / wait (and input for terminal games) only. Key names are pyautogui names: up, down, left, right, space, enter, esc, and single letters (r, w, a, s, d...). A wait uses 'seconds' (max 30).

If the manual says a control only works in a certain state (e.g. R only after game over, jump only when on the ground), add the inputs/waits needed to reach that state first. If that state cannot be reached reliably with simple inputs, mark the test not_testable and say why.
Set requirement_index to the plan requirement that mentions this control (zero-based); if none fits, use 0.
Do not write code, do not invent script_path values (use null), and do not add tests for anything other than controls.
